text:
amy_sales: Kicking off Cobalt POC — they report high time-to-first-token (TTFT) on hosted tests (median ~450-700ms, expected ~120-200ms). They also flagged security questions and pricing for a Dedicated option. Can we swarm?

devon_engineer: Can you share a sample request + model + sequence length? Also are they streaming or polling? Any client wrapper flags?

amy_sales: They used Redwood hosted, model=open-llama-13b-quant, prompt ~60 tokens, max_new_tokens=256, streaming=true. Sample request (redacted):

maria_support: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.app/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b-q","input":"<prefix>","max_new_tokens":256,"stream":true}'

aj_sre: Quick one: runtime logs show a lot of kv_cache.miss on first requests and an unusual header "X-No-Batch: 1" from their client, which forces microbatches of size 1. That plus streaming fragmentation explains higher TTFT.

devon_engineer: Right — streaming forces smaller microbatches to reduce time-to-first-chunk; combined with high max_new_tokens and concurrency that can increase overall TTFT. Two immediate mitigations: 1) temporary disable streaming for baseline TTFT tests; 2) enable prefix caching / warmup.

amy_sales: They need streaming for UX. Can we pre-warm and keep streaming? They have bursty traffic early in the session.

devon_engineer: Yes — pre-warm + prefix_cache helps. Recommend route config tweaks. Example:
```
route_config:
  prefix_cache: true
  cache_ttl_seconds: 3600
  batching:
    target_batch_size: 8
    max_latency_ms: 50
```
This keeps streaming but allows batching where possible. Also ask client to remove the X-No-Batch header.

aj_sre: Also seeing 429s from their upstream at ~50 RPS spikes — looks like a proxy/retry pattern. For a clean POC we can offer a small Dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbor throttles. Pricing question incoming.

jordan_sec: Security note: they want KMS integration and proof of no retention for POC. For hosted POC we can set data_retention_days=0 and disable logs retention, but they'll still want a SOC2 pack. I can send our standard questionnaire answers and a minimal KMS playbook for Private.

maria_support: I pushed a canary on staging with prefix_cache enabled and ran 4 parallel warmup calls. Observed median TTFT drop to ~150ms after warmup. Logs show kv_cache.miss for the first 1-2 calls, then kv_cache.hit.

devon_engineer: Nice. Tell them to avoid per-request random salts or timestamps in the prompt — that breaks prefix reuse. Also set client concurrency target to 4-8 to let batching work (not 1).

amy_sales: Action items: 1) warmup script -> Cobalt (maria), 2) quick Dedicated pricing estimate (aj), 3) send SOC2+KMS notes and NDA step (jordan), 4) share TTFT dashboard and keep monitoring (devon).

maria_support: Warmup script (run on client side):
```bash
for i in {1..6}; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.app/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b-q","input":"<stable_prefix>","max_new_tokens":32,"stream":false}' &
  sleep 0.2
done
wait
```
Run this 30s before traffic. It seeds KV and warms shared kernels.

aj_sre: For Dedicated pricing roughball: reserve a small pool (~1-2 p100-equivalent slots) starting at $15k/month for the POC tranche; will firm up with finance. Also recommend a short canary window with autoscale on.

devon_engineer: I'll make a short console dashboard share with TTFT histogram, batch sizes, and kv_cache hit rate. We should monitor `first_token_latency` and `batch_size_distribution`.

amy_sales: Cobalt's CTO wants to test now. Maria — can you drop the warmup script + instructions and I will coordinate the session?

maria_support: Dropped script to the Cobalt thread and pinged their engineer. Also set route flag prefix_cache=true on their POC route (canary).

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for route cobalt-poc @ canary-2024-07-08T14:09Z — health checks green.

aj_sre: Follow-up: I'll send a one-pager pricing note and a short diagram for Dedicated sizing. Jordan will follow the security questionnaire tomorrow.

amy_sales: Great work team — keep updates in this thread. I told Cobalt we'll remain available during their test window. :thumbsup:
